`abstract class BaseSelectorNode<V>`<br/>
**Extends:** [`BaseChoiceNode<V>`](/reference/controls/basechoicenode/)<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`SelectorNode`](/reference/controls/selectornode/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.ui.node.impl.control.selector` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [BaseSelectorNode.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/ui/node/impl/control/selector/BaseSelectorNode.java)

The behavior of a drop-down list without its look: a choice whose list opens on a left press and closes on the next one.

## Description

Extend [`SelectorNode`](/reference/controls/selectornode/) for a look made of a field and one node per option; extend `BaseSelectorNode` only to build the look entirely yourself.
While the list is open, a left press anywhere closes it; the list closes too when the selector is detached.

- [Controls](/use/learn/interactivity/controls/#choose-from-a-drop-down-list)
- [UI kit](/use/learn/going-further/ui-kit/#draw-a-control-entirely-your-own-way)

<a id="BaseSelectorNode-method-getOptionRank"></a>

### getOptionRank

`int getOptionRank(V value)` 

Returns the row of an option in the open list: `0` for the selected option, then the other options in their order, from `1`.

<a id="BaseSelectorNode-method-active"></a>

### active

`<T extends BaseSelectorNode<V>> T active(boolean active)` 

Gives the list its start state: `true` is open.

`<T extends BaseSelectorNode<V>> T active(Signal<Boolean> active)` 

Binds the open state to a signal both ways: the list follows the signal, and a press writes the new state into it.
Throws an `IllegalArgumentException` for a signal that cannot be written.

<a id="BaseSelectorNode-method-open"></a>

### open

`this open()` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Opens the list as if the user pressed the selector: `beforeOpen` can refuse it, then `onOpen` fires.

<a id="BaseSelectorNode-method-close"></a>

### close

`this close()` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Closes the list as if the user pressed it: `beforeClose` can refuse it, then `onClose` fires.

### beforeOpen

`<T extends BaseSelectorNode<V>> T beforeOpen(EventListener<NodeChangeEvent.Pre<T,Boolean>> listener)` 

Adds a listener that runs before the list opens on a press or `open()`; `cancel()` keeps it closed.

### beforeClose

`<T extends BaseSelectorNode<V>> T beforeClose(EventListener<NodeChangeEvent.Pre<T,Boolean>> listener)` 

Adds a listener that runs before the list closes on a press or `close()`; `cancel()` keeps it open.
